translationRepairs: He died in Guangda year 2 (567), aged sixty.
He died in Guangda year 2 (568), aged sixty.
s0075 光大二年 is Guangda year 2 (AD 568); the parenthetical 567 wrongly equates it with Guangda 1, and the proposed year is correct.
He also commanded the armorers and fought with merit in every engagement.
He also commanded troops and arms and fought with merit in every engagement.
s0047 兼統兵甲 means he also commanded troops and arms; "armorers" invents a craft guild the Chinese does not name.

He was then sent out with credentials as commander of the nine commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xin'an, Xinning, Xin'an, Jin'an, and Jian'an, general who guards the east, and administrator of Kuaiji.

He was then sent out with credentials as commander of the nine commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xīn'an, Xinning, Xìn'an, Jin'an, and Jian'an, general who guards the east, and administrator of Kuaiji.

s0069 lists distinct 新安 (Xīn'an) and 信安 (Xìn'an), so identical unmarked Xin'an spellings are a real error; tone marks distinguish the historical commanderies without translating their names or inserting Chinese graphs into the English prose.
He went south to Lingnan and entered the service of Liang's inspector of Guangzhou, the Prince of Xinyu, Xiao Ying.
He went south to Lingnan and entered the service of Liang's inspector of Guangzhou, the Marquis of Xinyu, Xiao Ying.
s0109 新渝侯 is Marquis of Xinyu (侯), not Prince; the proposed title restores the Chinese rank.
When Liang's Prince of Xinyu, Xiao Ying, held a commandery, Ke was called up as chief clerk.
When Liang's Marquis of Xinyu, Xiao Ying, held a commandery, Ke was called up as chief clerk.
s0144 likewise has 新渝侯; replacing Prince with Marquis corrects the same 侯/Prince mismatch.
He was sent out as cloud-banner general and administrator of Jinling, with middle two-thousand-dan rank.
He was sent out as cloud-standard general and administrator of Jinling, with middle two-thousand-dan rank.
s0126 雲麾將軍 is the cloud-standard generalship; "cloud-banner" misrenders 麾 and collides with 雲旗 wording used for a different title.
When the Founder moved against Wang Sengbian, he brought Leng, Hou Andu, and the others into council; Leng resisted the plan.
When the Founder prepared to kill Wang Sengbian, he brought Leng, Hou Andu, and the others into council; Leng resisted the plan.

s0114 誅 requires lethal intent that "moved against" softens, but completed "killed" misorders the council before the act (s0115–s0116 show fear of leaking the plan); "prepared to kill" keeps 誅 without false chronology.

When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Ke was further made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of armies in eighteen southern provinces including Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, general who guards the south, general who pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Ke was further made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of armies in eighteen southern provinces including Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, general who guards the south, Gentleman-General Who Pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
s0186 平越中郎將 is the Zhonglangjiang office, not a bare "general who pacifies the Yue"; the proposed title restores 中郎將.

When Emperor Xuan took the throne, [Ke] was additionally made Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Area Commander over Military Affairs in the eighteen prefectures of Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, General Who Guards the South, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

When Emperor Xuan took the throne, [Ke] was additionally made Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Area Commander over Military Affairs in the eighteen prefectures of Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, General Who Guards the South, Gentleman-General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
The literal of s0186 likewise drops 中郎將 from 平越中郎將; Gentleman-General Who Pacifies the Yue restores the full title.
It also sent Pei Zilie, lightning-might general, with five hundred horses to help Ke defend the river line.
The court also sent Pei Zilie, lightning-might general, with five hundred horses to help Ke defend the river line.
s0194 又遣 has an implicit court/state agent; dangling "It" is ungrammatical, and "The court also sent" matches the sense without adding unsupported detail.

He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff with Credentials, Area Commander over military affairs in the nine commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xin'an, Xinning, Xin'an, Jin'an, and Jian'an, General Who Guards the East, and Administrator of Kuaiji.

s0069 lists nine commanderies including both 新安 and 信安; untone-marked Xin'an twice conflates distinct places, and Xīn'an / Xìn'an correctly separates them.
He then traveled to Lingnan and served Liang's Inspector of Guangzhou, the Prince of Xinyu, Xiao Ying.
He then traveled to Lingnan and served Liang's Inspector of Guangzhou, the Marquis of Xinyu, Xiao Ying.
s0109 新渝侯 is Marquis of Xinyu (侯), not Prince (王); Prince of Xinyu invents a higher rank unsupported by the Chinese.
When the Founder killed Wang Sengbian, he drew Leng, Hou Andu, and the others into the planning, but Leng objected.
When the Founder prepared to kill Wang Sengbian, he drew Leng, Hou Andu, and the others into the planning, but Leng objected.
s0114 高祖誅王僧辯 is followed by counsel (引稜…共議) and s0115 懼其泄己 shows the killing is still only a plan; completed "killed" falsifies the chronology, while "prepared to kill" keeps the lethal sense of 誅.
He was sent out as Cloud-Banner General and Administrator of Jinling, with his salary raised to middle two thousand dan.
He was sent out as Cloud-Standard General and Administrator of Jinling, with his salary raised to middle two thousand dan.
s0126 雲麾將軍 uses 麾 as the military standard; Cloud-Standard General is the accurate title, and Cloud-Banner misrenders that office.
When Liang's Prince of Xinyu, Xiao Ying, was commandery general, Ke was summoned as chief clerk.
When Liang's Marquis of Xinyu, Xiao Ying, was commandery general, Ke was summoned as chief clerk.
s0144 新渝侯 again names Marquis of Xinyu; Prince of Xinyu is the same unsupported rank error as in s0109.
